newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat closes lower on commercial selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat closes lower on commercial selling.

text.p: CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed lower on commercial selling with a drop in soybeans also weighing on the market, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold 2.5 million bushels of July and Term Commodities sold one million bushels each of July and September, traders said.
The wheat market tumbled early despite early expectations for a firm tone. The fund long liquidation in the soybean pit was a key contributor to Wednesday's decline in the wheat market.
Wheat futures traders shrugged off early bullish input.
There was increased talk about the El Nino weather phenomenon this year. The El Nino was leading to concerns about dry weather in Australia's wheat growing region.
Seasonal harvest pressure added to the slide with the early stages of combining the soft red winter crop in Arkansas indicating good production prospects in that state.
CBOT soft red winter wheat futures closed unchanged to seven cents per bushel lower, with July down five at $3.38-3/4 and September closed seven lower at $3.45-1/4.
Damp weather slowed combining in Oklahoma but harvesting was expected to gain speed soon and there were reports this week of better-than-expected yields in some hard red winter wheat producing areas.

The market shrugged off news USDA said 100,000 tonnes of U.S. soft red winter wheat was sold to an unknown destination and took in stride news Morocco was seeking 50,000 tonnes of optional origin soft red winter wheat.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 15,000 contracts, above the 14,054 traded Tuesday.

In wheat options, Paine Webber bought 600 September $4.70 calls at 3/4 cent, ING Derivatives sold 600 July $3.40 puts at 2-1/2 cents and Smith Barney sold 200 July $3.60 puts at 19-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 7,000 contracts, below the 7,461 traded Tuesday.
